picks.headline: Full Game Preview and Score Prediction for Virginia Tech Football vs. SMU
picks.source: Virginia Tech Hokies On SI on MSN
picks.blurb: DALLAS — Virginia Tech football has a towering tilt on its hands today: SMU — the best opponent the Hokies have played all year. Virginia Tech (6-2, 3-2 ACC) became bowl-eligible after capturing a 20-16 victory over Clemson — its first over the Tigers since 2007 — and did not play this past week. SMU (6-2, 4-2 ACC) won six of its first seven games before a 30-27 stumble against Syracuse in the JMA Wireless Dome in Upstate New York. Both teams remain in contention for a spot in the ACC Championship Game and in the top-five unranked squads receiving votes for the AP Top 25, making Friday's contest particularly consequential as the regular season enters its final month. The Mustangs have been nearly untouchable at Gerald J. Ford Stadium, winning all five of their home games this season and each of their 11 ACC home contests since joining the conference in 2024. Virginia Tech, meanwhile, has already captured three road victories against Power Four opponents this season, including breaking its nearly-20-year drought against the Tigers. The Hokies and Mustangs haven't met since 1974, when SMU secured a 28-25 victory. More than five decades later, their first meeting as ACC opponents features two prolific quarterbacks and a pair of potent yet at-times inconsistent defenses. Here's a look at both teams ahead of Friday night's showdown. Virginia Tech's Offense Virginia Tech's offense has found its footing under quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer, who has completed 71.4% of his passes for 2,140 yards, 17 touchdowns, and just two interceptions through eight games. The Penn State transfer has provided a steady presence at center, throwing for at least 250 yards in five contests. However, the Hokies' offensive line has struggled to protect him at times, surrendering six sacks against Clemson. Grunkemeyer's top target has been wide receiver Que'Sean Brown, who leads the team with 685 receiving yards and three touchdowns on 51 receptions. Tight end Luke Reynolds has also emerged as a reliable option, collecting 50 receptions for 493 yards and a team-high six receiving scores. Reynolds caught the game-winning touchdown against Clemson, hauling in a fourth-and-1 pass with 1:44 remaining to put Virginia Tech ahead. On the ground, Jeffrey Overton Jr. has paced the Hokies with 639 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 113 carries, averaging 5.7 yards per carry. Marcellous Hawkins has added 337 yards and five rushing touchdowns, giving Virginia Tech another option out of the backfield. SMU's Offense SMU's offense has been one of the ACC's most productive units this season, averaging 35.3 points and 460-plus yards per game. Quarterback Kevin Jennings has been at the epicenter of that success, completing 73.7% of his passes for 2,414 yards, 21 touchdowns and five interceptions. The fifth-year signal-caller ranks among the nation's leaders in passing efficiency and surpassed 10,000 career passing yards in last week's loss to Syracuse. Jennings threw for 351 yards and two touchdowns against the Orange, but the Mustangs couldn't hold onto their late lead, conceding a game-winning Syracuse touchdown with 17 seconds remaining. Wide receiver Yamir Knight has been one of Jennings' primary targets, leading SMU with 523 receiving yards on 44 receptions and three touchdowns. Knight caught six passes for 80 yards and a touchdown against Syracuse. Running back Kendrick Raphael has provided balance to the Mustangs' passing attack, rushing for 692 yards and nine touchdowns on 135 carries. Raphael is no stranger to Virginia Tech, having scored three touchdowns against the Hokies last season while playing for California. His third touchdown tied the score late in regulation before Virginia Tech prevailed 42-34 in double overtime. Virginia Tech's Defense If Virginia Tech is going to leave Dallas with its seventh victory, its defense must make Jennings uncomfortable. The Hokies lead the nation with 77 tackles for loss and rank sixth nationally in sacks, having brought opposing quarterbacks down 27 times through eight games. Defensive end Aycen Stevens has spearheaded that effort with eight sacks, while defensive tackle Kemari Copeland has contributed four tackles for loss. Virginia Tech's defensive front was particularly disruptive against Clemson, accumulating 13 tackles for loss and four sacks while holding the Tigers to 16 points. In the secondary, cornerback Jaquez White delivered one of the game's defining plays, sacking Clemson's quarterback on the Tigers' final possession on a corner blitz. White finished with a team-high 11 tackles, helping Virginia Tech preserve its four-point advantage. Linebacker Keon Wylie has also been a consistent contributor, recording 41 tackles this season. The Hokies have been especially effective against the run, allowing just 93.4 rushing yards per game. However, their secondary has been less imposing, recording only two interceptions. Against a quarterback of Jennings' caliber, Virginia Tech's ability to generate pressure without exposing its secondary could prove decisive. SMU's Defense SMU's defense presents another difficult challenge for a Virginia Tech offense that has occasionally struggled with pass protection. The Mustangs have registered 22 sacks this season, led by defensive lineman Marques White's 5.5. Linebacker Alexander Kilgore paces the team with 41 tackles. SMU has been particularly effective on third down, allowing opponents to convert just 31 of 115 attempts — a 27% success rate that ranks No. 3 in the nation. The Mustangs have also been difficult to attack through the air, surrendering just 181.8 passing yards per game. Virginia Tech's ability to establish its running game with Overton and Hawkins could be particularly important, especially considering the Hokies were held to just 70 rushing yards against Clemson. Final Thoughts Friday's contest could come down to which team controls the line of scrimmage. Virginia Tech has made a habit of disrupting opposing backfields, but SMU possesses one of the most efficient quarterbacks in college football. Conversely, the Mustangs' pass rush will test an offensive line that has struggled to keep Grunkemeyer upright. The Hokies have already demonstrated their ability to win away from Blacksburg, but Gerald J. Ford Stadium presents a different challenge. SMU has yet to lose at home this season, and the Mustangs will be eager to respond after their disappointing trip to Syracuse. I think SMU will win but that it'll be far from easy. Kickoff is scheduled for 7 p.m. ET on ESPN. Ahead of the clash, here's our staff's predictions as to what will unfold tonight in the Lone Star State. JACKSON CAUDELL: While it will still be a long shot even if they find a way to win, the Hokies' ACC hopes are on the line tomorrow night at SMU. The Mustangs are also battling for their ACC title hopes, and that makes this a fascinating matchup. This is a chance for James Franklin to land another win against one of the better programs in the conference, and I think they have the offense to take advantage of a suspect SMU defense. If the Hokies can get after Kevin Jennings and force a few turnovers, I think they are able to do that and score a big win. Final score prediction: Virginia Tech 31, SMU 27 JAMES DUNCAN: Syracuse left a blueprint last Saturday, beating SMU 30-27 on a touchdown with 17 seconds left. Virginia Tech is built to follow it. Nobody has beaten the Hokies by more than five points this season, and they come in with 13 days of rest to SMU's six. Ethan Grunkemeyer has thrown 17 touchdowns and two interceptions, and both picks came in one night against Pitt. He won't hand Kevin Jennings free possessions, which puts the game on Brent Pry's defense. That group made 13 tackles for loss at Clemson, and it won't need half that many Friday if it gets off the field on third down. Friday won't be a rout, but I think the Hokies give the Mustangs their first home loss in the ACC. Final score prediction: Virginia Tech 30, SMU 28 THOMAS HUGHES: Let's get this out of the way: SMU has never lost an ACC game at home. Its strongest wins at Gerald J. Ford Stadium this season, however, came against Virginia and California - two squads with a combined 7-11 (4-8 ACC) record. The Hokies should be well-equipped to contend with the Mustangs, though SMU signal-caller Kevin Jennings may present Tech with its toughest test of the season yet. Virginia Tech quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer has been stellar this campaign, throwing 17 touchdowns to just two interceptions, and while I expect another strong performance from him, I think SMU narrowly edges Virginia Tech in Dallas tonight. Final score prediction: SMU 31, Virginia Tech 28 KADEN REINHARD: I think this game will be defined by one word over the 60 minutes of action: Intensity. Several factors will fuel that fire: Friday night lights, the Mustangs coming off the Syracuse loss and Tech finding itself back in the receiving-votes category of the AP Top 25. But most importantly, I see both offenses locking into a close-knit battle, as both sides can mend their attacks with a healthy mix of the ground and air attack. Ultimately, I think the Hokies' defense can handle the contest by not allowing SMU quarterback Kevin Jennings to extend many plays outside the pocket, which has been a struggle for the Hokies in recent years. Meyers had never scored for the Orange before that catch. The touchdown beat SMU 30-27 and knocked the Mustangs out of the AP Top 25. Virginia Tech should have that clip on a loop. The Hokies (6-2, 3-2 ACC) visit SMU (6-2, 4-2) at 7 p.m. ET Friday on ESPN. The Mustangs are 5-0 at Gerald J. Ford Stadium this season and 6.5-point favorites. Their defense holds up better against the pass than the run, and its injuries are stacked in the middle of the field. Two of my predictions start there. The third starts with what Syracuse did to Kevin Jennings. 1. Luke Reynolds has his best game since September SMU doesn't give much away through the air. Opponents complete 62.6% of their passes and average 6.0 yards per attempt. The one real hole is at safety. Sophomore Tyren Polley Jr., third on the team with 34 tackles, tore a pectoral muscle in October and is out for the season. SMU has played two games without him: a 59-20 win over Cal and the loss at Syracuse. Help could be coming. Ahmaad Moses, a first-team All-ACC safety in 2025, is questionable after missing the whole season while SMU works on his eligibility. The junior tight end has 50 catches for 493 yards and six touchdowns, and his 50 catches lead all FBS tight ends. The last three games have been quieter: 13 catches for 120 yards since Pitt. Two of those 13 went for touchdowns at Clemson, including the go-ahead score in the fourth quarter. Friday, he clears 100 receiving yards for the third time this season and finds the end zone again. 2. Jeffrey Overton Jr. snaps his 100-yard drought Overton last reached 100 yards on Sept. 26, when he ran for 209 at Boston College, the sixth-highest single-game total in Virginia Tech history. He has 230 yards in four games since and averaged 2.6 yards per carry at Clemson. The sophomore still leads the Hokies with 639 yards on 113 carries. Two things change Friday. The first is the offensive line. "We're going to get some guys back, which is helpful, especially on the offensive line," coach James Franklin said Monday. Guard/tackle Montavious Cunningham and guard Brody Meadows are expected to play. Left tackle Justin Terry is still out. The second is the defense across from him. SMU allows 125.9 rushing yards per game and 3.8 yards per carry. Those numbers flatter the Mustangs. College football counts sacks as rushing plays, and SMU has 23 sacks for 148 yards. Pull them out, and opponents are averaging 4.8 yards per designed run. Those 23 sacks matter for Virginia Tech in another way. Ethan Grunkemeyer has been sacked 23 times himself. A run game that works keeps the Hokies on schedule and gives SMU's rushers something else to think about. Overton gets his third 100-yard game of the season. 3. Virginia Tech sacks Kevin Jennings at least four times Before Halloween, SMU hadn't allowed more than two sacks in a game this season. Syracuse got six. Look at who was playing on the left side. True freshman Drew Evers moved over from right tackle to start at left tackle, and fellow true freshman Sam Utu made his first career start beside him at left guard. It was only the second college game of his career. SMU could get some help back. Guard Alex Woods, a starter, missed Syracuse, and tackle Andrew Chamblee, who has started at both tackle spots, hasn't played since Oct. 17. Neither is on Thursday's availability report. Watch the first series to see who lines up on the left. Either way, Virginia Tech has the rushers to test it. The Hokies average 3.4 sacks per game, sixth in FBS, and three players have more than four: Aycen Stevens with eight, Cortez Harris with five and Mylachi Williams with 4.5. Defensive tackle Kemari Copeland said this week the plan is to "cage" Jennings and take away his scrambles to the right. Friday, the Hokies get to Jennings at least four times. away.headline: Virginia Tech injury report for Stanford paints a promising outlook for Justin Terry
away.blurb: In the Hokies Week 3 35-26 victory over Maryland, Virginia Tech lost offensive lineman Justin Terry in the first half, and he has been out since then. However, there could be some light at the end of the tunnel for Terry in terms of getting back onto the field, and it might come as soon as this upcoming weekend when Stanford visits . That certainly would be a positive, but a return on Saturday night feels a little ahead of schedule. It would be surprising if he were rushed back from an injury to play against the Cardinal. Franklin said that Terry will likely be a game-time decision. "It's not like we're totally through it," Franklin said. "We still got the rest of the week, and probably will come down to either a game-time decision, or it will be he's cleared, but we still don't feel like he's gotten enough reps." Three regular-season games remain in the 2026 campaign, and already at 6-3, the Hokies are guaranteed a bowl game later next month before the attention shifts toward the 2027 season. Getting Terry back would be a big addition, but even if he does return this weekend, his snaps might be limited; just his presence would be big for Grunkemeyer and the rest of the offense. Virginia Tech football comes out of bye week getting healthier in one pivotal area Going all the way back to the summer, injuries along the offensive line have been an issue for first-year Virginia Tech football coach James Franklin. Then, it carried over into the regular season, where it seems that when it rains, it pours. James Franklin gives positive Justin Terry injury update ahead of Stanford game According to Andy Bitter of Tech Sideline , Terry was going through 1-on-1 drills with the D-linemen. After practice, Franklin gave an update on his linemen ahead of Stanford visiting on Saturday night at Lane Stadium. "So today was really the first day that we've been able to have him for everything," Franklin said , per Virginia Tech Athletics ' YouTube . "We've been kind of working him in slowly. Drills, (individuals), one-on-ones. So today was the first day we've kind of had him for everything. So he's getting closer, and it's positive for us.'' Virginia Tech's offensive line can use all the help it can get If and when Terry comes back, it'll be a welcome sight for Hokies fans. To say that the offensive line has struggled this season would be an understatement. Some of that is because of injuries, while some of it is because there have been guys moved around to different positions. Consistency is key and it feels like there hasn't been much of it this season. Virginia Tech has struggled to protect quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer at times, despite the Penn State transfer having a good year statistically. Then there is the running game that the Hokies have desperately tried to get going. away.blurb: The player availability report, which was first used for the 2025 season, provides five types of designations prior to game day: available, probable, questionable, doubtful, and out. A player being available means that they are not designated on the list. Here's how the availability report shakes out by position: This article was originally published on www.si.com/college/virginiatech as Initial Availability Report Released for Virginia Tech-Stanford: Who's In, Out, TBD For Hokies? . BLACKSBURG — After a 23-point loss to SMU in Dallas, Virginia Tech football takes on Stanford in a Saturday night showdown in Lane Stadium. Ahead of the clash, the ACC revealed the initial player availability report for both teams this week. Here's the list of players posted on the initial availability report, organized by status: Offensive Line: 4 (Wright, Austin, Bright, Terry) Wide Receiver: 2 (Peterkin, Stuewe) Virginia Tech (6-3, 3-3 ACC) opened its season with four straight wins for the first time since 2017, defeating VMI (73-3), Old Dominion (44-21), Maryland (35-26) and Boston College (21-14). The Hokies claimed their largest margin of victory since 1922 with their 70-point win over the Keydets Sept. 5, and they avenged their loss from Sept. 13, 2025, against the Monarchs which forced the ouster of then-head coach — and Virginia Tech's current defensive coordinator/linebackers coach — Brent Pry one day later. Against Maryland, the Hokies broke a 15-game Power Four non-conference losing streak dating back to 2017, beating the Terrapins by nine. Sept. 26's victory in Boston College was harder to come by, but amid a nor'easter, sophomore running back Jeffrey Overton Jr.'s career-high 209 rushing yards proved enough for the Hokies to escape with the victory. The Hokies sustained their first loss on Oct. 2, falling to Pitt 35-33 after conceding a 35-10 run over two-plus quarters. Virginia Tech made a nine-point rally to pull within two, but fifth-year kicker John Love's 36-yard field goal attempt for the win was ruled no good. The Hokies lost to Cal 25-20 in Berkeley the following week, ceding the game-winning touchdown to the Golden Bears with 18 seconds remaining. Virginia Tech returned to the win column on Oct. 17, defeating Georgia Tech 34-24 in a contest where it led 24-3 at intermission. The Hokies then became bowl eligible with a 20-16 win over Clemson — their first over the Tigers since 2007 in their trip to Memorial Stadium since 2012. Virginia Tech, however, fell in a 51-28 blowout at SMU Nov. 6, allowing season-highs in both points (51) and total yards of offense (569). The 51 points the Mustangs totaled on Virginia Tech were the most allowed by a Hokies team since the 2021 Pinstripe Bowl against Maryland, while the 569 yards Tech allowed were the most since Oct. 10, 2020, against North Carolina. The Utes have cruised to an 8-0 record, winning six of their eight games by at least two touchdowns. Last week, they thrashed Cincinnati 49-25 behind 534 yards of offense. BYU has been shaky since stunning Notre Dame in Provo, losing in double-overtime to UCF and only beating lowly Arizona State by one touchdown last week. BYU dominated the LaVell Edwards era, winning 19 of 21 matchups. Then starting in 2002, the rivalry moved heavily towards the Utes, with a 14-3 mark. BYU has now won three straight since 2021, including both matchups as members of the Big 12 by a combined four points. The 2026 game could be an all-time classic. The sophomore has thrown for 1,750 yards, rushed for 336 yards and scored 19 touchdowns. In an upset of Notre Dame, Bachmeier passed for, rushed for and caught touchdowns. No. 7 BYU visits No. 3 Utah on Saturday, November 7, in the first Holy War where both teams are ranked in the top 10. The 10 a.m. local kickoff at Rice-Eccles Stadium adds another wrinkle. Utah is 8–0 and sits atop the Big 12 at 5–0. BYU is 7–1 and shares second place with Texas Tech, but its loss to UCF leaves little room for error. Utah opened as roughly a 5.5-point favorite with a total of 48.5. These predictions go against the safe script, a ground-game surprise, a Utah quarterback performance and a late BYU rally that falls short. Let's take a look at the bold predictions for this marquee matchup. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) LJ Martin plays, but Bear Bachmeier is the star Rob Gray-Imagn Images LJ Martin will return and play a limited role, yet Bachmeier will be the one who carries BYU's offense. Martin has missed four games with a leg injury and has not played since the October 3 win over TCU. He is still BYU's leading rusher at 344 yards and 7.8 yards per carry, so the Cougars badly need him. But offensive coordinator Aaron Roderick said Martin is "not all the way back yet," which suggests a managed workload. The prediction is Bachmeier throws for 275 yards and rushes for two touchdowns, outproducing Martin in every category. Bachmeier has already accounted for most of BYU's rushing output without Martin, with 336 rushing yards and seven rushing touchdowns on 80 carries. He also has 1,750 passing yards and 12 touchdowns. Utah's secondary is among the best in the country, so BYU may need Martin's presence as a decoy more than as a workhorse. That could open play-action and RPO looks for Bachmeier. Devon Dampier and Wayshawn Parker combine for 300 total yards Utah's offense will hinge on its quarterback and running back, and together they will account for 300 total yards and four touchdowns. Dampier has been outstanding, with 12 total touchdowns against one interception over his last four games. He has completed 69.6 percent of his passes for 1,876 yards and 18 touchdowns this season. Parker is the other half. He has 726 rushing yards and nine touchdowns, and Utah's ground game ranks eighth nationally at 226.9 yards per game. BYU's rush defense is strong in raw yardage, ranking 20th at 100 yards per game, but Covers notes it ranks only 74th in rush success rate. That gap suggests Utah can win with misdirection and efficiency instead of pure power. The Utes also rank third nationally in third-down efficiency at 54.1 percent, which helps them sustain drives against an aggressive linebacker group. Utah will lose right tackle Kelvin Obot for the season, but the line has still been one of the best in the country. I expect the Utes to handle his absence. Utah wins 31–27 and snaps BYU's three-game streak The final prediction is a four-point Utah win that comes down to the last possession. BYU has won three straight in the series, while Utah had won nine in a row before that. Utah has still won 14 straight overall, the longest active streak in the FBS. Utah's offense should control the game early, but BYU will keep it close by converting in the red zone. A late Cougars touchdown will make it a one-possession game before the Utes' defense finishes with a stop. The projected 58 total points would clear the 48.5-point line comfortably. The point spread would also come down to a single score, giving BYU a cover as a 5.5-point underdog. The result would leave Utah in prime position for a Big 12 title game berth and a playoff bid. BYU would stay alive in the conference race, but it would have almost no margin left. No. 9 BYU @ No. 3 Utah This Holy War might be the holiest of them all: Utah hosting bitter rival BYU, with the winner in the driver's seat for a Playoff spot. It’s the first time both teams have been ranked in the top 10 for this matchup, and I can’t wait to start the day with this one. I think BYU might win outright. It has been tested with its win over Notre Dame just a few weeks ago. Yes, it lost to UCF the following week in a typical trap game — big home win followed by a road conference game. Otherwise, the Cougars have handled business, even though the scores don’t seem that impressive. BYU is built on defense. It is 13th in yards per play and it limits explosives. It does not rush the passer all that well, but against Utah’s rushing attack, that might not be needed. BYU’s defense already faced a high-powered offense in the Irish and limited it to a negative EPA rushing day. Utah’s offensive production slowly ticked down when conference play started, but it did bounce back last week against a poor Cincinnati defense. Utah has played one defense in the same realm as BYU and that was Houston. Utah struggled to score, only putting up 21 points with seven of those happening super late after forcing a Houston turnover. Will the BYU offense find a groove against Utah? (Getty Images) It’s fair to also believe BYU’s offense might struggle in this game. However, it appears the Cougars are getting stud running back LJ Martin back, and they are much better when Martin is on the field. He’s averaging almost eight yards a carry with 20% of his rushes going for 10+ yards. Utah’s defense is the typical physical front against the run, but BYU is the best offense the Utes have faced all season. Utah’s pass rush concerns me. It is 80th in pressure rate and unless it blitzes, it isn't able to get to the quarterback. Seems less than ideal against BYU quarterback Bear Bachmeier. I see these teams as even. They are both defensively based with an offense that wants to run the ball. That’s too many points in a game like this. I’ll take BYU to cover. Schwartz's Pick: BYU -4.5 No. 5 Alabama @ No. 14 LSU In the newly-released CFP rankings, Alabama is fifth and is an underdog at LSU by almost a touchdown. I do lean towards LSU at -6, but that number feels big. Instead, I’m going to fade Alabama’s offense in this game. Alabama is facing its fourth straight difficult defense, and in the first three games, we’ve seen the offensive efficiency drop. Quarterback Keelon Russell is nearing the end of his first season as a starting quarterback, and he’s been mostly excellent for his age. However, he has struggled the last three weeks outside the end of the Texas A&M game. Against Georgia, Tennessee and A&M, he completed only 60% of passes with just four passing touchdowns and three interceptions. Alabama’s beat-up offensive line has allowed 11 sacks in the three previous games. Now, the Tide play an LSU defense that’s first in sacks per pressure and 11th in pressure rate. The Bama offensive line and Russell were noticeably affected by the environment in Tennessee, and now they are at LSU. I feel most comfortable with Alabama not scoring much in this game. The Tigers (6-2, 3-2 SEC) have already blown out league foes Florida and Texas A&M at home this season and are 13-3 at Faurot Field against league opposition since 2023. Taking on Texas (6-2, 3-2) represents an uptick in competition, but the Tigers shouldn't be lacking confidence. Florida was No. 8 in the AP poll when it arrived at Mizzou on Oct. 3. It left with a 45-17 loss that legitimized Missouri and showed its full potential. Since then, we've also seen Missouri's floor, which was found in a 31-3 loss at Ole Miss on Oct. 17. But after a bye week and a 34-10 "get right" win over Arkansas in Week 9, the Tigers appear to be back on track. The Longhorns are entering off wins over Ole Miss and Mississippi State , but their vaunted offense is still falling short of expectations. Is this the point when everything will start to click for quarterback Arch Manning ? If a Texas team that spent four weeks at No. 1 earlier this season is going to meet expectations, a breakthrough needs to come soon. Where to watch Texas vs. Missouri live Date : Saturday, Nov. 7 | Time : 12 p.m. ET Location : Faurot Field -- Columbia, Missouri TV: ESPN | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Texas vs. Missouri: Need to know Injuries mount for Texas: Injuries are adding up for the Longhorns, who enter this matchup with star receivers Ryan Wingo and Cam Coleman listed as questionable. Wingo is dealing with a quad injury while Coleman is working through a shoulder issue. Both have appeared in all eight games for Texas up to this point while combining to catch 11 of Arch Manning's 15 touchdown passes. Star edge rusher Collin Simmons is also questionable after missing Texas' past two games because of an ankle injury. That's a lot of star power in the "questionable" category for Texas. By contrast, Missouri's injury report is nearly clean. Welcome back, Ahmad: Missouri running back Ahmad Hardy made his 2026 debut last week, carrying the football twice in the Tigers' win over Arkansas. The 2025 All-American has been on the mend from a gunshot wound, and his return adds to a running back room that already features the SEC's leading rusher. Jamal Roberts became the conference's first back to surpass 1,000 yards for the season while rushing for 138 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries in a win over Arkansas. Roberts surpassed 200 yards in wins over Florida and Texas A&M last month. Gaining traction against Texas will be tough. No team has averaged more than four yards per rush attempt against Texas. College Football playoff implications: Texas' chance to reach the College Football Playoff will improve to 67.5% with a win, according to the CBS Sports CFB Forecaster. They will drop to 22.8% with a loss. If the Longhorns lose, they would need to win out against LSU, Arkansas and Texas A&M in order to potentially reach the 12-team field as a three-loss team. Missouri's chances to make the CFP will improve to 16.1% with a win. Those hopes would crater to 1.6% with a loss. The Tigers close with Georgia , Kentucky and Oklahoma . Texas vs. Missouri prediction, picks The best unit on this field is the Texas defense. Regardless of the health status of star edge rusher Collin Simmons, the Longhorns should be able to slow down a Missouri offense that hasn't faced a swarming unit of this caliber. If Arch Manning can just take care of the football like he did last week, Texas can lean on its defense, win the field position battle and put stress on a Missouri defense that showed real vulnerability in losses to Mississippi State and Ole Miss. The Tigers have been great at home the last few years, but they are a rung below Texas in overall talent level. Staff Picks and Scores Skip to main content SI.COM LONGHORNS NEWS 2025 Football Bracket FOOTBALL FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS 2023 FOOTBALL COMMITS SI.COM LONGHORNS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM LONGHORNS BB After getting to play their entire October slate in the Lone Star State, the Longhorns are once again leaving town for Columbia, Missouri, to take on the No. 18 Missouri Tigers. While fans may already be looking ahead to next week's highly anticipated Death Valley matchup, the Tigers are certainly not a team to overlook . They're coming off a 34-10 blowout win over Arkansas — albeit, it was against the Razorbacks — and steamrolled the same Florida team that stunned Texas with a second-half comeback just a few weeks ago. Saturday's matchup carries significant postseason implications , both for the College Football Playoff and the SEC championship race, as both teams enter with identical 3-2 conference records. Here’s how the Texas Longhorns On SI Staff sees this one playing out. Matt Galatzan Texas has gotten back on track over the last two weeks, but various shortcoming are still very prevelent. Texas has struggled along offensive line, and as a result, the running game has suffered. Those issues have also caused a cascading effect on the passing game, making for an inconsistent product. To make things worse, things on the injury front don't look good for the Horns. Kade Phillips, Ryan Wingo and Graceson Littleton are all banged up but should play, while Colin Simmons and Cam Coleman are less likely to play, and Hollywood Smothers and Nick Townsend were both lost for the year. Texas can overcome these issues if the defense continues to perform at a high level. Ole Miss showed the blueprint to shut down the Tigers ' offense. If Texas can stay on schedule on offense and avoid a third-quarter collapse, I think they can get it done. Texas 27, Missouri 20 Phoenix Haigis Texas has started to find their groove again with two major wins at home against Ole Miss and Mississippi State. The Longhorns now go back on the road against another ranked opponent in Missouri. As much momentum as Texas has going into this game, all the advantages matchup-wise go in favor of the Tigers. Texas is dealing with a significant amount of major injuries with the addition of running back Hollywood Smothers being out for the season while Missouri will see their running back Ahmad Hardy return for the first time this season. The Tigers are one of the best teams at home this year and have the best turnover margin in the SEC against a Lorghorns team that has had turnover issues this season. picks.blurb: Greg McElroy Predicts Missouri Upset That Could Shake Texas' Playoff Hopes Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS ESPN analyst Greg McElroy believes Texas’ turnover problems will catch up with the Longhorns at Missouri, making the Tigers his lone outright upset pick of Week 10 as both 6-2 SEC teams fight to stay in the College Football Playoff race. McElroy backed the Tigers on his Always College Football podcast, predicting a low-scoring game decided by ball security. “The team that gives it away just one time, that’s the team that’s going to lose,” he said. Why is Greg McElroy picking Missouri? Missouri Tigers head coach Eli Drinkwitz reacts toward a referee during the first quarter against the Mississippi State Bulldogs | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect “Missouri is +8 in turnover margin. Texas is -3,” McElroy said. “That’s probably the clearest season-long difference between these two teams.” “Missouri is +8 in turnover margin. Texas is -3,” McElroy said. “That’s probably the clearest season-long difference between these two teams.” The Tigers turned four Arkansas turnovers into 24 points in last week’s win in Fayetteville, and Missouri coach Eli Drinkwitz said afterward that “turnovers are the name of the game .” McElroy added that Missouri has scored 62 points off takeaways this season without allowing a point off a giveaway. “So when his team wins the turnover battle by one or more, Eli Drinkwitz is 39-4,” McElroy said. Texas checked in at No. 7 in the first College Football Playoff rankings , 11 spots ahead of Missouri. Still, both Missouri losses came on the road against Mississippi State and Ole Miss, two teams Texas beat over the last two weeks. Arch Manning’s costly turnover trouble Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning (16) looks on after a medical check during the game against Ole Miss | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Texas quarterback Arch Manning has 15 touchdown passes and averages 8 yards per attempt, but McElroy flagged his seven interceptions as a problem against a team that “cashes mistakes in very, very quickly.” Both Texas losses came by three points and turned on fourth-quarter turnovers, including a pick-six against Oklahoma and a strip-sack with under two minutes left against Florida. Texas quarterback Arch Manning has 15 touchdown passes and averages 8 yards per attempt, but McElroy flagged his seven interceptions as a problem against a team that “cashes mistakes in very, very quickly.” Both Texas losses came by three points and turned on fourth-quarter turnovers, including a pick-six against Oklahoma and a strip-sack with under two minutes left against Florida. Mississippi State sacked the redshirt junior six times last Saturday, and Texas now plays without left tackle Trevor Goosby, who suffered a season-ending knee injury against Ole Miss. “They average getting sacked nearly one out of every 10 dropbacks,” McElroy said of Texas. “That’s 126th because the breakdowns come from all over the protection.” The ESPN analyst said Texas has struggled when its receivers have to beat man coverage snap after snap, and he called Missouri’s cornerbacks “about as good as you find when it comes to playing that coverage week in and week out.” How does Texas reach 24 points? Texas Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian celebrates with fans and players after the game against the Mississippi Rebels | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect McElroy questioned how Texas coach Steve Sarkisian’s offense gets there. “When his team scores fewer than 24 points, Steve Sarkisian is 14-35,” McElroy said. “And Texas already goes three-and-out on more than a quarter of their possessions.” McElroy questioned how Texas coach Steve Sarkisian’s offense gets there. “When his team scores fewer than 24 points, Steve Sarkisian is 14-35,” McElroy said. “And Texas already goes three-and-out on more than a quarter of their possessions.” The Longhorns’ running game offers little relief, with McElroy saying their backs “are getting hit almost as soon as they take the handoff.” Running back Hollywood Smothers is out, and receivers Ryan Wingo and Cam Coleman were both listed as questionable on Thursday’s SEC availability report . Wingo, a St. Louis native Missouri recruited out of high school, leads Texas with 36 catches for 470 yards, while Coleman, an Auburn transfer, leads the team with seven touchdown catches. McElroy’s route to 24 points runs through Wingo “in the catch-and-run game” against a Missouri defense he said sits “at or near the bottom as far as missed tackles,” plus “one Coleman shot over the top.” “But without it, Texas might be living on field goals, which is a dangerous recipe on the road,” McElroy said. A loss would send Texas to LSU next week with three defeats, a scenario ESPN analyst Paul Finebaum said could cause the Longhorns to “ collapse .” Texas visits Missouri at noon ET Saturday on ESPN. picks.blurb: Expert Picks: Longhorns Wire staff predict Texas vs. Missouri - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL news, live updates Misiorowski, Schlittler win Cy Youngs NFL midseason awards Rex Ryan arrested Skubal suitors emerge Expert Picks: Longhorns Wire staff predict Texas vs. Missouri Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 7 Texas and No. 18 Missouri have only met once on the football field since the Tigers left the Big 12 along side Texas A&M for the SEC. That meeting was the 2017 Texas Bowl. What should scare Longhorns fans is the 2026 version is tinkering on the edge of a disappointing bowl like that. Especially if they can't beat a team like Missouri. The Tigers are a good team. It's easy to see Missouri winning on Saturday. They're ranked just 11 spots below Texas in the College Football Playoff rankings and have the same record. And Mizzou has home field advantage. Then why is Texas a -3.5-point favorite. Because a fully functioning Texas team is better than Missouri. But this Texas team isn't fully functioning. First, the injuries are starting to pile up. It was announced this week that the Longhorns have lost running back Hollywood Smothers and tight end Nick Townsend for the rest of the season. All-American right tackle Trevor Goosby is also out for the year. And UT has been without All-American EDGE Colin Simmons for weeks. In addition to trying to plug the injury holes, Texas coach Steve Sarkisian must also continue to work on the offense. At times it looks great. But its not trustworthy. Will Muschamp's defense will need to stand tall for a third game in a row if the offense can't get it going. Tommy Bresee's Prediction Texas walks into this Missouri game needing the win to feel confident about their CFP chance heading into LSU. Missouri is a relative unknown, with losses to both Mississippi schools but a dominating win over Florida. Jamal Roberts and the run game leads the way, averaging just over 160 rushing yards/game. Austin Simmons has become a riser in this upcoming NFL Draft, flashing his elite arm talent every week. Texas was able to get a win over Tennessee earlier this season, but I don't see this as a task that's comparable. Missouri is capable of performing at a high level on both sides of the ball, especially the front seven defensively. It's difficult to imagine this Texas offense to trade punches with Missouri, especially on the road, so I'll take the Tigers to possibly end Texas' CFP hopes. Final Score: Texas 20, Missouri 23 Jamie Gatlin's Prediction The Longhorns will take on Missouri this Saturday in their latest SEC clash. The Tigers are off to an impressive 6-2 start and, like Texas, are 3-2 in conference play. Texas will need Arch Manning to be at his best and for the defense to shine. Last week, the Longhorns defense held Mississippi State to three points and 187 total yards. If the Longhorns can replicate that performance, another win could be on the horizon. This should be a game that Texas can win as they look to improve their playoff odds. Final Score: Texas 31, Missouri 13 Trey Luerssen's Prediction When this year's schedule came out, I thought the game against Mizzou might be the toughest to forecast. But it's even tougher now, because we're not sure which team will actually show up on either side of the ball. Both teams have had some big wins and some real clunkers. How much will Texas miss Smothers and Townsend? Can the defense slow down the Tigers offense? Which version of quarterback Arch Manning will show up in Columbia? For four games in a row, Texas has jumped out to an early lead and then coughed it up by the end of the third quarter. UT is 2-2 in that stretch. A coin flip. Twice the dam broke and twice it didn't. I think the defense will save the offense again. picks.blurb: It’s Tigers versus Longhorns in a top-20 battle. No. 19-ranked Missouri football will take on No. 9/10 Texas this coming Saturday, Nov. 7, on Faurot Field in a top-20 matchup that will have significant implications on the College Football Playoff race in the SEC. Mizzou (6-2, 3-2 SEC) doesn’t have much more — if any — margin for error this year, and Eli Drinkwitz looks likely to have essentially his full roster available for the huge home game. Texas (6-2, 3-2) is coming off back-to-back wins over Ole Miss and Mississippi State, which were MU’s two losses this year, and holds the No. 7 ranking in the initial CFP top 25. Here’s what Mizzou fans need to know about the Longhorns, as well as a score prediction for the Nov. 7 game: How does Missouri defend Texas QB Arch Manning? Mizzou has to get consistent pressure on Arch Manning. No quarterback in the SEC has been sacked as many times as Manning. No QB has thrown as many passes considered “turnover-worthy,” at least in Pro Football Focus’ accounting, while under pressure than the Texas QB’s seven. There’s been a boom-or-bust element to Manning’s play when rushers get into his space. Not only has he thrown seven turnover-worthy passes on those plays, but he’s thrown an SEC-high nine “Big Time Throws.” Quite often, he’s taking a shot with some degree of difficulty or deep downfield when pressure arrives at his doorstep. Perhaps more importantly, though, will be coverage sacks. Manning is happy to wait for routes to develop, even if it means he’s taking a hit. The longer the Tigers’ defensive backs can stay attached to their assignments, giving the QB fewer options to bail the offense out with big throws, the better. Can Mizzou keep turnover margin in its favor? Missouri keeps winning the turnover battle. The Tigers are averaging a +1.3 turnover margin per game this year, which is tied for the sixth-best mark nationally. Texas, meanwhile, is 94th in the country, giving the ball away more per game than it is taking it away. The Longhorns, at -2.0, actually have the third-worst turnover margin in the FBS in road games this year. Manning has recorded the eighth-most fumbles in the country this season. He’s also thrown seven picks, three of which were while he was under pressure, per PFF. There aren’t many stats that translate to winning football games like creating and avoiding turnovers. “Turnovers are the name of the game,” Drinkwitz said after MU’s win at Arkansas, where his team forced four. Texas has been a little prone to giveaways, so the more hits the Tigers can land on Manning, probably the better. Texas injury concerns The Longhorns’ injury report had a number of notable names Wednesday night to open the gameweek. Three defensive starters were listed as questionable, including star defensive end and future first-rounder Colin Simmons. Texas also listed starting nickel Graceson Littleton and corner Kade Phillips as questionable to face Mizzou. Two starting wide receivers join those players on the 50/50 list: Ryan Wingo and Cam Coleman. The Longhorns have ruled out rotational running back Hollywood Smothers and starting left tackle Trevor Goosby. Is this a CFP elimination game? The first College Football Playoff rankings of the 2026 season arrived Tuesday with Mizzou checking in at No. 18 and Texas at No. 7. That gives us a good idea of what the committee thinks of two teams that have identical records (6-2, 3-2 SEC). The Tigers need some quality wins — and fast. They’ll get chances. In the next three weeks, Drinkwitz’s team faces CFP-ranked No. 7 Texas, No. 2 Georgia and No. 6 Kentucky. It’s possible that a 9-3 team from the SEC sneaks into the playoff. Likely, at this point. But is it Mizzou? The path to that record, which at least puts MU in the conversation, probably requires a win over Texas. Georgia on the road, after all, is next. That ain’t easy. Texas at No. 7 is a different story. It’s tough to tell exactly what the committee is thinking, but checking in that high says that the committee values wins over Ohio State, Tennessee and Ole Miss. The Longhorns could maybe afford a loss to MU, provided it then turns around and beats LSU, Arkansas and Texas A&M down the stretch. There’s a lot of football to play, but this is a fascinating game in the scope of the year. Score prediction: Missouri 24, Texas 20 This game could come down to how well Mizzou runs the football. The Texas defense has elite athletes up front, even if players like Simmons can’t go, and the Tigers cannot afford to struggle on the ground like they did against Ole Miss. If that happens, the Longhorns are running away with this one. But if Jamal Roberts and Ahmad Hardy can help MU control the clock and open up some space for Austin Simmons through the air, the Tigers have a really good chance for a memorable day at Memorial Stadium.

However, there are four games remaining, and the first one up is a top-25 matchup on the road against the No. 18 Missouri Tigers. So, as the Horns look to cement their place in the postseason, what should we expect, and what are oddsmakers expecting, out of Texas? Well, despite the Horns struggling against lesser opponents throughout the season, and despite the fact that it's a road game for them, head coach Steve Sarkisian and his squad are favored in Columbia this Saturday. Final spread, moneyline, and total for No. 7 Texas at No. 18 Missouri Spread: -2.5 Texas, +2.5 Missouri Moneyline: -142 Texas, +120 Missouri Over-Under: +/-42.5 points While the spread hasn't changed throughout the week, with the Horns idling as 2.5-point favorites , the point total has dropped from the initial 44.5-point expectation. Now, the over-under is set at just 42.5 points, giving a nod to the two teams' defenses over their offenses and setting the final score somewhere in the ballpark of 22.5-20, with the Horns walking away victorious. For understanding the moneyline, one simply can't overthink what the numbers mean. If someone bet $142 on the Horns winning, they would walk away with a $100 profit. Keys to Longhorns defeating the Tigers in Week 10 So, in order for the Longhorns to pull off that narrow victory (or, hopefully, by a larger margin) over Missouri? Well, for starters, with both starting wide receivers Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo possibly missing from the lineup, quarterback Arch Manning is going to have to either (1) connect with new downfield targets or (2) continue to use his legs more. Similarly, the Texas offense will have to lean on the run game, which has been hit or miss this season, despite the fact that the team's original RB1, Hollywood Smothers, has been sidelined for the season with a torn MCL. So, Raleek Brown and supporting running backs Michael Terry III and Derrek Cooper Jr. will have to step up to the plate to carry the load out of the backfield. The Horns are also struggling with injuries on the defensive side of the ball, possibly opening up the air-raid offense for the Tigers and quarterback Austin Simmons. However, even with the nation's top defensive player, Colin Simmons, still sidelined, Texas has continued to dominate at the line of scrimmage. In other words, this might be an even lower-scoring game than Vegas oddsmakers are expecting, especially if Texas struggles to find its footing right away on offense. away.headline: Texas's initial injury report provided sweet relief ahead of Longhorns' trip to LSU
away.blurb: While defensive tackle Hero Kanu was listed as questionable after suffering a shoulder injury in Texas's Week 10 win over the Missouri Tigers, many of the Horns' previously questionable players were already off the first availability report of the week: OUT: Hollywood Smothers (RB), Trevor Goosby (OL), Nick Townsend (TE), Richard Wesley (EDGE) Meanwhile, the Tigers' first availability report for Week 11 also didn't include quite as many stars for LSU, other than the fact that star linebacker Whit Weeks was listed as "questionable" and not definitively out: OUT: Dashawn Spears (S), Phillip Wright III (WR), Charles Ross II (LB), Richard Anderson (DT) PROBABLE: Gabriel Reliford (DE), Weston Davis (OT) The return of Weeks could spell trouble for Texas's already-shaky offensive line, and the absence of defensive tackle Richard Anderson and linebacker Charles Ross II doesn't exactly provide much reprieve, with neither seeing significant playing time throughout the season so far. In other words, both teams would be pretty close to full strength, or at least as close as possible with a couple of players out for the season. So, no matter which team wins, the other wouldn't be able to point to injuries as the reason for its loss. Over the last few weeks, the Texas Longhorns have seen some of their key players go down in games and subsequently pop up on the team's availability reports . That has included stars like edge rusher Colin Simmons, wide receivers Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo, and defensive back Graceson Littleton. Well, as the Horns' Week 11 matchup against the LSU Tigers has come into focus, Texas was luckily able to remove quite a few of those crucial players from its injury list. In fact, when Steve Sarkisian and the Horns released their initial availability report on Wednesday evening, it included some of the best news possible ahead of the top-25 SEC game. Texas Longhorns' Week 11 initial availability report vs. LSU Tigers Simmons, Coleman, Wingo, Littleton, Kade Phillips, and other stars (on both sides of the ball) were finally off the injury list from the jump, a great sign of the Horns' ability to rehabilitate their players to full health. Of course, the recurring presence of running back Hollywood Smothers and offensive tackle Trevor Goosby should come as no surprise, with both suffering season-ending knee injuries in the last month. LSU Tigers' Week 11 initial availability report vs. Texas Longhorns The continued absence of safety Dashawn Spears has been a burden for the LSU secondary over the last 10 weeks. Similarly, wideout Phillip Wright III hasn't seen the field since the Tigers' second game of the season. home.blurb: "We were very fortunate. When you watch it, it looks bad, but the cleat was not in the ground, which is a real relief there," Mizzou head coach Eli Drinkwitz said Tuesday. "So, anticipate him trying to practice today, and we'll monitor that situation as it goes. … He was out in practice yesterday (Monday), and he is probably as tough a competitor as I've been around, so nothing would shock me more than if he wasn't playing. But, again, I don't know how his body will respond to that injury." The Tigers did, as expected, rule out defensive end Langden Kitchen, who Drinkwitz said Tuesday had surgery on his knee after sustaining an injury during the Tigers' loss to Texas this past Saturday. Kitchen will not play for Mizzou again this season. As it has since SEC play started, Mizzou ruled out running back Malae Fonoti, who is out for the season, right tackle Josh Atkins, who Eli Drinkwitz said he does not expect to be available this year, and tight end Gavin Hoffman. The possible designations, from most likely to play to least likely, are as follows: available; probable; questionable; doubtful; out. The reports are not technically injury reports, which some teams — Mizzou often included — provided in years prior. Instead, they are lists that include any players ruled unavailable or possibly unavailable for upcoming games. That could be for any number of reasons, including but not limited to injuries. home.headline: Texas's final injury report provides a slight reprieve for the Longhorns vs. Missouri
home.blurb: With one brutal injury list after another, it looked like the Horns could be without as many as eight or nine starters. Luckily, in Texas's final availability report ahead of kickoff, it looked like the Horns might actually catch a break as a few players shifted toward being available. On Friday night, defensive backs Kade Phillips and Graceson Littleton were both listed as "probable" after spending a majority of the week under the "questionable" category, as was wide receiver Ryan Wingo. However, as most injury reports go, it was not all good news for Texas. We have known for a couple of weeks that starting left tackle Trevor Goosby was out for the rest of the season, but starting running back Hollywood Smothers joined him on that list after tearing his MCL. Additionally, edge rusher Richard Wesley and tight end Nick Townsend were both on the availability report, once again, as "out." Then, star edge rusher Colin Simmons was listed as "questionable" for a third straight week after suffering a high-ankle sprain against the Florida Gators in Week 7. Wide receiver Cam Coleman joined Simmons in the grey area after getting beat up against Mississippi State last week. On ESPN's College GameDay , Pete Thamel reported that the two were "game-time decisions," with Simmons seeing a larger likelihood of suiting up and actually setting foot on the field. OUT: Trevor Goosby (OL), Hollywood Smothers (RB), Nick Townsend (TE), Richard Wesley (EDGE) QUESTIONABLE: Colin Simmons (EDGE), Cam Coleman (WR) PROBABLE: Ryan Wingo (WR), Kade Phillips (DB), Graceson Littleton (DB) While any injuries are far from ideal, the final availability report of the week was far from the worst news for the Longhorns. Yes, a few stars are still out or doubtful, but it also looked like quite a few would be available in the top-20 SEC matchup. OUT: Malae Fonoti (RB), Josh Atkins (OL), Gavin Hoffman (TE) Last week saw the return of Missouri's star running back Ahmad Hardy, who had suffered a gunshot wound to the leg this offseason. While he did not see many reps in Week 9, one could expect his workload to increase as the Tigers and the Longhorns clashed. No. 7 Texas and No. 18 Missouri are scheduled to kick off at 11 a.m. CT on Saturday, Nov. 7, and the game will be available on both ABC and fuboTV. With a win, the Horns could take one more step toward cementing their place in this season's College Football Playoff. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 5 Alabama is out to defend its College Football Playoff ranking, while No. 14 LSU seeks to remain in the hunt Getty Images One of the best modern-day rivalries in college football headlines on Saturday when No. 5 Alabama and No. 14 LSU meet in Baton Rouge for the 91st meeting in the series. The Crimson Tide hold a 58-27-5 advantage overall, but it's the 13-2 record in the past 15 meetings that has given them the upper hand in a battle between programs that would otherwise be considered peers. This is, after all, set to be the 25th time that both schools are inside the top 15 of the AP Top 25 poll and with Alabama's recent crowning as a top-five team in the College Football Playoff rankings, there's even more ranked-on-ranked intrigue. LSU is hoping that the home field advantage of Death Valley can play a role in the game, as the Tigers are 32-3 in their last 35 home games in Tiger Stadium. Speaking of streaks, the game also presents LSU coach Lane Kiffin with a chance to finally defeat Alabama as a head coach. The former Crimson Tide offensive coordinator lost to Nick Saban once as Tennessee's head coach in 2009, then four times between 2020-23 as Ole Miss ' head coach, when they were SEC West division rivals. That 0-5 record against the Crimson Tide, paired with LSU's recent struggles in the series, provides plenty of extra motivation for the home team looking to roar back into the playoff race. Where to watch Alabama vs. LSU live Date : Saturday, Nov. 7 | Time : 3:30 p.m. ET Location : Tiger Stadium -- Baton Rouge, Louisiana TV: ABC | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Alabama vs. LSU: Need to know Alabama's injury report will be an X-factor: There will be key updates throughout the week, perhaps all the way up to warm-ups, that will determine the health of the Crimson Tide and their ability to perform to the expectations of their top-five rating. Starting center Racin Delgatty has missed multiple games while dealing with injury, and his absence has been noticeable on an offensive line that has cooled off since putting up 49+ points in consecutive wins against Florida State , South Carolina and Mississippi State . The Crimson Tide have failed to record 70+ rushing yards as a team in each of their last two games and allowed 21 sacks in SEC play, which ranks 14th among 16 teams in the league. Alabama will also be looking for updates from star wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams and cornerback Zabien Brown , adding to the unknowns for how the Tide will stack up against LSU. LSU passing attack rounding into form : No one in the SEC had a more productive passing attack in the month of October than LSU, which averaged 339.5 passing yards across all four games last month. The Tigers went 3-1 across those games, only losing to top-10 Kentucky by one point in Lexington on a walk-off two-point try. LSU now leads the SEC and ranks tied for 7th nationally on the season, averaging 318.0 passing yards per game, and the improvements have come with both Sam Leavitt's improved play and the emergence of Jackson Harris as a go-to receiver. A transfer from Hawaii , Harris played three whole games before scoring his first touchdown of the season but has exploded ever since with seven touchdown catches across the last five games. That includes four multiple-touchdown games and a yards-per-reception average (17.6) that ranks 4th among all SEC pass catchers. After being dismantled at home by the Alabama Crimson Tide , reaching the coveted post-season seems unlikely in year one of the Lane Kiffin era, and there is another top-ranked team waiting just around the corner for the Tigers. Having already fallen in the AP Pol l, to nearly on the outside looking in, where will the Tigers find themselves in the second College Football Playoff rankings ? With two losses already on the year heading into the first set of College Football Playoff rankings, the Tigers' room for error was minimal, and their ranking reflected that, coming in at No. 14. A win over the Crimson Tide would have put the Tigers in a comfortable position for the rest of the year, especially given the rest of the schedule remaining. Instead, with three losses, their ranking will plummet during the second release. Despite the loss, the Tigers shouldn't fall out of the top 25, as the committee has proven it won't shy away from ranking three-loss teams. Three were ranked last week: the South Carolina Gamecocks, the Oregon Ducks, and the Florida Gators. The Tigers should, at a minimum, replace the Gators, who suffered a fourth loss of the season this past weekend. The Missouri Tigers, who were also ranked and lost a third game of the season, should fall, but they also played a closer game against the top-ranked Texas Longhorns. Your previews: Alabama gets an immediate chance to justify its CFP ranking, while LSU can strengthen its argument with a win that leaves the Tide staring at three losses. I picked LSU to win this game in August, and I'm sticking with the Tigers' passing game at home against an Alabama secondary still sorting through injuries. LSU wins 26-20, keeping its SEC title hopes alive and giving Alabama fans another reason to avoid the internet. Alabama football needs this win. Kalen DeBoer wins after idle weeks. It's a unit starting to find itself after single-score losses to Ole Miss and Kentucky. LSU has the second best scoring offense and defense in the SEC. It has the No. 1 total offense and defense in the SEC. This is a Tigers team that is waiting for an opportunity to see what it can do against the upper echelon of SEC play in November, and the Crimson Tide is the first team in LSU's way. Alabama has looked like the best team in the country before on the road, beating Mississippi State to a pulp in Starkville, but the same couldn't be said about Kentucky in Lexington, or, especially, Tennessee in Knoxville. Expect the Crimson Tide to falter against LSU. It's an afternoon game instead of an ultra-amped up night showdown in Death Valley, but it shouldn't matter too much that the Tiger fan base is just a little less … prepared. Yeah, Ole Miss, Kentucky, and Auburn are, arguably, the three best teams LSU faced, which is why those road games were tough, but LSU hasn't even let the opponents breathe at home, winning all five games by a combined score of 225-44 with the closest game a 35-6 win over Texas A&M. LSU won't destroy Alabama, and it'll be a back-and-forth fight, but there will be that moment in the second half when it all clicks, and the Tigers will put the game away with a sharp scoring drive. The crowd will take over from there. They now enter Week 10 ranking first in the entire country in net adjusted EPA per play, seventh in net yards per play, and seventh in net success rate. That's a step above Alabama, which ranks fifth, 15th, and ninth in those three metrics. The one weakness that LSU has is stopping the run, ranking just 54th in opponent EPA per rush, but unfortunately for the Crimson Tide, they haven't run the ball efficiently this season, ranking just 50th in EPA per rush. Without the ability to take advantage of LSU's biggest weakness, this is going to be a tough road game for Alabama. I'll lay the points with the Tigers. We have a third of the starting lineup listed as questionable, and we saw what happened in Knoxville when none of those guys played. Word is that Alabama expects to get some key players back, but will they be 100%? On top of that, Keelon Russell has struggled at times against the blitz this season, and will be facing one of the most blitz-happy teams in the country. It does appear that LSU will be without MLB Whit Weeks, so that will help. Still, this is perhaps the most hostile environment in the sport, against a team that leads the SEC in both offense and defense, that also happens to need this win to get into the playoff discussion after Tuesday night's rankings dropped. Sure, they are in this position because they lost at Ole Miss and Kentucky, but those were road games. Still, we Gump to a standard around here. The one thing that Alabama can point to is Sam Leavitt's propensity to turn the ball over, and Alabama's defense has been as opportunistic as any in the country. We're going to say that the bye week afforded Russell the opportunity to learn from film study, and Alabama will get just enough guys back to get it done in Red Stick as they have so many times in the past. Tiger head coach Lane Kiffin predicted Thursday that the junior wideout will play, but that isn't guaranteed. Coleman-Williams can provide an explosive play threat whenever he's on the field. Against Tennessee, that lack of explosives was obvious, and contributed to the loss. That same thing can't happen in Tiger Stadium. Even if its superstar receiver can't go, Alabama has to find some big plays on offense. Lotzeir Brooks is a threat, as is Rico Scott. LSU leads the SEC in rushing defense, allowing only 2.7 yards per carry and 85 yards per contest. None of this will be easy. That's about it for today. Have a great weekend.

Both teams are heading into the high-stakes matchup after a rested bye week as both teams work on their list of player injuries. The game's outcome could decide both teams' fates in the playoffs, creating an anticipated matchup in the long-standing rivalry. Here are three bold predictions for LSU's matchup against Alabama. Trey'Dez Green Will Be Alabama's Biggest Target LSU Tigers tight end Trey'Dez Green (7) celebrates his touchdown catch as Auburn Tigers take on LSU Tigers at Jordan-Hare Stadium in Auburn, Ala. on Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026. LSU Tigers lead Auburn Tigers 31-10 at halftime. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect LSU is able to recover from some of its injuries, including tight end Trey'Dez Green , who returns after missing four of the team's mid-season games. Green appeared in the team's defeat over Auburn, putting up 50 receiving yards across five receptions and a touchdown. Green ended up leaving the game early, after head coach Lane Kiffin reported that Auburn's defense was attempting hip drop tackles on the talented tight end, a move that significantly increases a player's chances of getting injured and one that was banned in the NFL in 2024. While he may not be getting targeted in the same way against Alabama, he still will have all the pressure on him, making him a risky target for Leavitt, who's already struggled with turnovers this season. The 6'7, 237 lb. tight end is the ultimate weapon on offense, one that Alabama has experience in facing, being aware of his ability to contribute to the Tigers' offensive success and making all the moves to limit it on Saturday. LSU's Defense Will Hold Keelon Russell To 170 Passing Yards Oct 24, 2026; Tuscaloosa, AL, USA; Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell (12) leaves the field after the Crimson Tide win at Saban Field at Bryant Denny Stadium. Alabama defeated Texas A&M 31-20. Mandatory Credit: Gary Cosby Jr.-Tuscaloosa News | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect LSU's defensive unit, one of the best groups in the league, will face a major challenge against Alabama's offense, led by quarterback Keelon Russell . Russell is also anticipating the obstacle of the Bayou Bandits, a team that has allowed 172.8 passing yards from opponents per game. Limiting Russell to the magic number of 170 passing yards will prove its ability to hit Alabama where it hurts, putting pressure on its offensive leader. During the team's back-to-back losses this season against Georgia and Tennessee, Russell put up a season low of 147 passing yards during the trip to Neyland Stadium, scoring the only touchdown for the Tide during the game. Against the Bulldogs, Russell still couldn't hit the 200 mark, ending the loss with 185 passing yards. Now that he will face one of the league's most dangerous defenses, a unit that once held the most sacks this season, Russell's passing production could take another major blow if the defense can keep up the pressure all game long. LSU Will Record 5+ Sacks Oct 24, 2026; Auburn, Alabama, USA; LSU Tigers defensive end Princewill Umanmielen (1) sacks Auburn Tigers quarterback Byrum Brown (17) during the second half at Jordan-Hare Stadium. Mandatory Credit: John Reed-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect LSU's defense can limit Russell's production from the first snap, closing in on him in the pocket and recording more than five sacks against the Tide quarterback. He sits in the Top-10 for the quarterback with the most sacks this season, recording a staggering 22 so far. Against LSU's defense - a unit that met the program's record for the most sacks in one game during Week 2 of the season - Russell and his offensive line could be in major trouble. This production will come from the exterior of the line, with defensive end Princewill Umanmielen becoming Russell's biggest nightmare as the leader of the defense with nine sacks so far. Even if the Crimson Tide can put extra pressure on Umanmielen's side, defensive end Jordan Ross brings the same threat on the opposite end, as major pressure will be closing in on Russell all game long. LSU Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin walks on the sideline during the first quarter against the Kentucky Wildcats at Kroger Field. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect College Football Playoff hopes will be on the line Saturday. LSU and Alabama would love to notch a signature win. Alabama's opportunistic secondary could trouble Sam Leavitt and the offense. If Leavitt protects the ball and the defensive line takes advantage of a potentially vulnerable Crimson Tide offensive line, LSU should win. Tiger Stadium will be deafening, and I think the Tigers will make a statement on Saturday. LSU 35, Alabama 24 I think that the Tigers win a close one at home. This freshly healthy Alabama squad will be a tough challenge for these LSU Tigers, but I think that the LSU defense will come up with a pick-six late in the game to seal their victory. LSU 31, Alabama 28 LSU and Lane Kiffin are ready to take down Alabama. For Kiffin, he's 0-5. For LSU, a three-year losing streak will end. Sam Leavitt has made the jump and taken care of the football and looked sharp through the air, with LSU having solid o-line play to lead the way in establishing the run and attacking Alabama's defense in every way. The Tigers' defense is ready for the challenge too. With Alabama missing some key pieces on the o-line, and LSU's dominant pass rush, the matchup easily favors the Tigers. With the home-field advantage, I think LSU will be able to gain the momentum early, and Alabama will lose key momentum in the environment of Tiger Stadium. LSU 28, Alabama 20 While LSU vs. Alabama isn't a "storied" rivalry, it's perhaps some of the best football that gets played each year, and this matchup will be no different. Kiffin is looking for his first signature win with LSU, and if Sam Leavitt continues to play the same way he has the last two weeks, I expect it to happen. Despite the fact that they have a really good quarterback in Keon Russell, I do think that the vital piece of their offense being missing will affect their game this weekend. I also think that our defense is a lot stronger than theirs is; we are holding opponents to fewer points per game than their team is, despite both defenses being really good. In terms of our offense, I think that Sam Levitt has been on the up and up the past couple of games; he hasn't thrown any interceptions, and he's looking more like the 2024 CFP quarterback that he once was. home.blurb: LSU football defensive end Gabe Reliford was listed as probable for the Texas game on LSU's Wednesday injury report. If Reliford plays, it would be a quick, impressive return from an ACL tear suffered in spring practice. Reliford is yet to suit up in 2026. LSU's defensive end duo of Princewill Umanmielen and Jordan Ross is one of the best in the SEC. Still, Reliford's return would be welcomed, as he provides a physical, bruising presence against the run. With Reliford out, Dylan Carptenger emerged as LSU's core third defensive end and has given Blake Baker's defense valuable reps. Even if Reliford does go, it remains to be seen how he'd factor into the rotation. He's a capable player, but this would be a big spot to return to given how much time he's missed. Anything LSU can get from the third-year defensive end is a positive, though, given it looked like he would miss the entire year after the injury occurred in the spring. LSU's entire defense has been impacted by the injury bug this year. Safety Da'Shawn Spears tore his ACL vs. Ole Miss and is out for the year. Linebacker Whit Weeks has been out since Week 4. home.headline: Whit Weeks and another injured LSU defender could return for Texas game, according to SEC report
home.blurb: Whit Weeks and another injured LSU defender could return for Texas game, according to SEC report By JON BLAU | Staff writer Jon Blau Weeks was categorized as “questionable” for the Tigers’ game against Texas in the Southeastern Conference’s initial release for the week. The senior defender has been sidelined since he suffered a lower-leg injury against Texas A&M on Sept. 26. Weeks was listed as “doubtful” on multiple SEC availability reports in the days leading up to last week’s game against Alabama. The senior was inevitably ruled out the Friday night before a 31-13 loss. LSU could also return another injured defender this Saturday, because defensive end Gabriel Reliford, who suffered an ACL tear in March during spring practice, was listed as probable for the Texas game. LSU coach Lane Kiffin previously said it was unlikely Reliford would return to play this season. Right tackle Weston Davis, who was knocked out by an injury versus Alabama, was also listed as probable for Texas. A listing of “questionable” is supposed to confer that an athlete has about a 50% chance of suiting up for that week’s game. “Doubtful” means closer to a 25% chance — and an “out” designation means a player has been ruled out completely. Aside from Weeks, LSU is without safety Dashawn Spears, receiver Phillip Wright and linebacker Charles Ross, who have all suffered season-ending injuries. But the Tigers remain relatively healthy otherwise, especially since tight end Trey’Dez Green’s return. Freshman defensive tackle Richard Anderson, who missed the Auburn and Alabama contests, was also listed as out on Wednesday’s report.
