On his podcast, "See Ball Get Ball" , Pollack explained how he thinks the No. 2 Georgia at No. 10 Ole Miss game will unfold. Pollack emphasizes that Georgia will try to establish the run to keep Chambliss off the field. He thinks Chambliss' legs will play a big role in the red zone. "I don't think this game will be like it was in Athens last year," Pollack said. Georgia beat Ole Miss 43-35 at home and consistently moved the ball. "I don't think it's going to be where you score every possession. I do think there'll be a lot more stops." Pollack thinks Georgia will have to run Stockton a good amount. He thinks Georgia learned their lesson from last season and do a better job of keeping Chambliss in the pocket. Pollack trusts the team of Georgia. "I do trust the team of Georgia to to to overcome to be better," Pollack said. He predicts that Georgia will win 28-24, which would be a major step for Georgia in the SEC championship and College Football Playoff race. "Hasn't mattered," Pollack said on Ole Miss running back Kewan Lacy being out for the Georgia game. "They've been good without Kewan." away.blurb: Missouri wide receiver Cayden Lee was not listed on the first SEC Student-Athlete Availability Report on Wednesday. This means he is available to suit up in the contest. Lee endured a knee injury in the fourth quarter against Texas after taking a hard hit, but coach Eli Drinkwitz announced that there was no structural damage Tuesday. Drinkwitz cited the toughness of Lee in the press conference and sounded rather optimistic about his return. "He was out in practice yesterday and he is probably as tough a competitor as I've been around, so nothing would shock me more than if he wasn't playing. But again, I don't know how his body will respond to that injury," Drinkwitz said. Drinkwitz announced Tuesday that starting edge Langden Kitchen would be out for the remainder of the season. After suffering a knee injury early in the game against Texas, Kitchen had surgery Tuesday morning, per Drinkwitz. So when the injury report came out, as expected, Kitchen was listed as out. Alongside the starting edge rusher, the Tigers are without Malae Fonoti, Josh Atkins and Gavin Hoffman. The three Tigers have been out for the entirety of SEC play. away.blurb: But the Bulldogs have been struck by injuries at critical positions the last two seasons in the CFP. In 2024, Georgia football starting QB Carson Beck suffered a season-ending injury in the SEC Championship Game - paving the way for Gunner Stockton to make his first career start against Norte Dame in the Sugar Bowl. That injury coupled with turnovers turned out to be too much for the Dawgs to overcome. Only two players are listed on Georgia football's injury report - DL Josh Horton and LB Amaris Williams. Williams was expected to be out, but Horton is a new addition to the injury repot. Horton is listed as questionable for the contest; Williams is listed as out, which means he will not play in the contest. Meanwhile, Missouri has four players listed as out: DL Langden Kitchen, RB Malae Fonoti, OL Josh Atkins and TE Gavin Hoffman. It should be noted that Ole Miss QB Trinidad Chambliss is listed as probable for the Rebels' game this weekend at Oklahoma. He joins a a list of 17 other Rebels on the injury report after Georgia's 42-7 beating of Ole Miss in Oxford. The Dawgs, on the whole, continue to be pretty healthy in the grand scheme of things. Should Isiah Canion and Chauncey Bowens return to full health the Bulldogs could become even lethal on the offensive side of the ball. Coach Kirby Smart said earlier this week that Bowens was not 100% healthy. Meanwhile, it will be curious to see if Amaris Williams will return this season. He suffered an ALC injury in the spring, and although the timeline would be tight, it is not out of the question that he could return to play in the playoffs the same way WR George Pickens did at the end of the 2021 season. Pickens also had an ACL injury around the same time that year. home.headline: Kewan Lacy Injury Update, Latest on Ole Miss Star's Status, Return Timeline amid CFP Bracket Push
home.blurb: Lacy missed time with a shoulder injury earlier this season before suffering a dislocated shoulder in an Oct. 24 game at Texas. He had already been ruled out of Saturday's matchup at Oklahoma. The running back was listed as the No. 21 prospect on Bleacher Report's 2027 NFL draft big board back in September. Lacy is eligible to either enter the draft or return for another college season in 2027. Saturday will mark Lacy's third straight absence. He will also be expected to sit out an Oct. 21 matchup against Wofford and the Oct. 27 regular-season finale against Mississippi State. Icon Sportswire/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images College Football Trinidad Chambliss and Ole Miss will have to continue their push for the College Football Playoff without star running back Kewan Lacy. On3's Pete Nakos reported Thursday Lacy is expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season due to injury. CFB Overreactions after Week 10 😲 Scouts have only gotten to see Lacy play the majority of a single college season. After appearing in six games as a true freshman at Missouri, Lacy joined Ole Miss in 2025 and went on to lead the FBS with 306 carries. Lacy paced the SEC with 24 rushing touchdowns during that sophomore season to go with 1,567 rushing yards over 15 games. Injuries have kept Lacy from replicating that campaign as a junior. He will finish the 2026 season with 78 carries for 388 yards and five scores. Lacy's injury issues started when he suffered what Ole Miss coach Pete Golding called a "bruised" left shoulder last December during a first-round CFP win over Tulane. He remained with the Rebels for the rest of their run to the CFP semifinals and later underwent offseason surgery on his shoulder. Lacy suffered a thigh injury in Ole Miss' season opener against Louisville, then rnjured his shoulder Sept. 19 against LSU. The running back missed one contest before returning to the lineup, only to suffer his next shoulder injury three games later. Ole Miss (6-3) fell nine spots to No. 19 in the second CFP selection committee rankings after a blowout loss to No. 2 Georgia last Saturday. That defeat left the Rebels with no room for error as Ole Miss works to convince the selection committee this team still deserves a playoff spot in Chambliss' last college season. The Ole Miss Rebels are 6-3 overall and 4-3 in SEC play after their brutal 42-7 loss to Georgia last weekend in Oxford. Two weeks before that, they fell 34-27 at Texas. Those are two ranked opponents who are firmly in the College Football Playoff Conversation, but it's too late in the season to be dropping games like that. Now they head into a crucial SEC clash at Oklahoma on Saturday, with the CFP potentially hanging in the balance. More news : Brian Kelly Sends Blunt Warning to Texas Ahead of LSU Clash Lacy quickly emerged as one of the best players in college football last season, rushing for 1,567 yards (third most in FBS) and 24 touchdowns (second) on an FBS-leading 306 attempts, averaging 5.1 yards per carry, along with 177 receiving yards. He earned first-team All-American and first-team All-SEC honors, and entered this year on the preseason watchlist for several national awards. But Lacy injured his left shoulder in the Rebels' loss to Texas on Oct. 24, and hasn't been able to recover. His third, and potentially final, college season ends after just six games, finishing with 388 rushing yards and five rushing touchdowns on 78 carries (5.0 yards per carry). Makhi Frazier, a Junior transfer from Michigan State, and sophomore Shekai Mills-Knight will continue to handle the bulk of the carries for Ole Miss. Frazier has 365 rushing yards on 72 carries this season (5.1 yards per carry), while Mills-Knight has 165 yards and three touchdowns on 33 carries (5.0 yards per carry). Pete Fiutak · College Football News Sat, November 7, 2026 at 2:18 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads When we last saw Oklahoma and Florida play, the Sooners rolled 55-20 in the 2020 Cotton Bowl over a high-powered Gator team that lost to eventual national champion Alabama in an epic SEC Championship. The other meeting was the BCS Championship at the end of the 2009 season, when Tim Tebow and the Gator defense took down Heisman-winner Sam Bradford and the amazing Sooner attack 24-14 for the national title. The stakes aren't as high this time around, but for a Florida program that's on the rise, and No. 24 in the first College Football Playoff rankings, and for a 4-4 Oklahoma desperate to close strong, this will be intense. Oklahoma vs Florida: Quick Hits Oklahoma at 4-4, needs to win two of its last four to be bowl eligible. It hosts Ole Miss and Texas A&M after this before closing at Missouri. Florida is coming off the 27-8 loss to Georgia. It goes to Kentucky next, hosts Vanderbilt, and finishes at Florida State. Again, the first two meetings were in big bowl games. This is the first regular season matchup between the two. How To Watch Oklahoma vs Florida Date: Saturday, November 7, 2026 Game Time: 7:45 PM ET TV: SEC Network Location: Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, Gainesville, FL – Week 10 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Expert Picks: Week 10 Why Oklahoma Will Win The defense continues to fight the good fight. It had a problem in the 42-25 loss to South Carolina, but the defense is fantastic on third downs thanks to a pass rush that takes over games. But to beat Florida, you have to slow down the run. The Gators are 0-3 when running for fewer than 155 yards, and the Sooners give up just 107 yards per game. Only Mississippi State and, last week, South Carolina have been able to gash the Sooners for more. Why Florida Will Win Oklahoma's offense has a hard time running the ball. With a defense as good as the Sooners have, all the O has to do is keep it moving and not screw it up. But no running game means more pressing overall, and then come the mistakes. The Sooners only average 107 yards per game on the ground, and they just can't find any room to move. The Gators have to hold up, and then pounce on an Oklahoma attack that turned it over four times against both Georgia and Kentucky, three times against New Mexico, and twice against Michigan. Oklahoma vs Florida Prediction, Betting Lines It's stupid, but if you buy into these things, going back to the last two games of last season, Oklahoma is on a ten-game run of alternating wins and losses. The Sooners beat Texas, then lost to Kentucky, beat Mississippi State, lost to South Carolina, beat … Florida? The Sooners have the defense to hold up and make Florida struggle. The Gators got by Texas a few weeks ago, but it's been a struggle, losing three of the last four. Weird trends aside, this Oklahoma team really does have a way of rallying when it absolutely has to. picks.headline: Staff Picks: Will Oklahoma Get Back on Track at No. 24 Florida?
picks.blurb: Staff Picks: Will Oklahoma Get Back on Track at No. 24 Florida? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL news, live updates Misiorowski, Schlittler win Cy Youngs NFL midseason awards Rex Ryan arrested Skubal suitors emerge Staff Picks: Will Oklahoma Get Back on Track at No. 24 Florida? Oklahoma Sooners tight ends coach Jason Witten will take over as interim offensive coordinator for the rest of the season. | Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Ryan Chapman · Oklahoma Sooners On SI Fri, November 6, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Gators have an impressive resume, having beaten No. 4 Ole Miss 52-28 at The Swamp, then going on the road to Austin and taking down No. 7 Texas 27-24 - one week after OU beat them in Dallas - on a night the underwhelming Florida defense overwhelmed Arch Manning and the Longhorns, sacking him five times, limiting UT to 2-of-10 on third down (they had 13 first downs total) and holding the Horns to 272 total yards. But they were also blown out in back-to-back losses to No. 25 Missouri and unranked South Carolina, which preceded last week's 27-8 loss to No. 3 Georgia. Oklahoma is a touchdown underdog to Florida, but the Sooners are the best defense the Gators face. Still, OU may be reeling after its worst defensive performance in years in the blowout loss to South Carolina - which included an incomprehensible 25 missed tackles (usually 10 is a bad number). OU's first trip to The Swamp will be punctuated by another big game from Gators RB Jaden Baugh, who's third in the SEC at 100.3 rushing yards per game and first with 13 rushing TDs. Final score: Florida 28, Oklahoma 21 Things could get gross Saturday night. Florida has officially made a quarterback change, and Tramell Jones Jr. could be without a pair of key weapons to pair with an already banged up offensive line. Oklahoma's offense has been so bad it got its coordinator fired, but Jason Witten has never called plays collegiately and John Mateer is still likely the quarterback the Sooners will roll with. OU's defense needs to bounce back after its tackling struggles last week, but even an improved showing could see Gator running back Jaden Baugh have enough success to push Jon Sumrall's team across the finish line. Final: Florida 16, Oklahoma 13 OU is set up for further disaster as it heads to the swamp. Jason Witten will serve as the Sooners' play caller for the first time at the college level, John Mateer is still the quarterback and Ben Hill Griffin Stadium is one of the nation's most hostile atmospheres. But amid the weirdness, I expect OU to win this game. Teams often come out more inspired after a notable firing, and I predict Witten will lead a creative game plan as he auditions for the full-time offensive coordinator role. Florida's offense is good - but it is also prone to turning the ball over. If the Sooners are able to put pressure on Tramell Jones Jr. early, it will create a long day for the Gators' offense. Final: Oklahoma 24, Florida 20 The Sooners figure to get a little boost from Jason Witten's playcalling, but don't expect massive changes in either scheme or production here. The offensive line still has its issues, John Mateer hasn't been consistent at all, and neither of the other quarterbacks have experience in games like this. But Oklahoma's defense does figure to have a bounce-back game after struggling to contain LaNorris Sellers and the South Carolina offense. The tackling will be better, and Florida's offense is in a bit of flux itself with Tramell Jones Jr. expected to make his second start of the season at quarterback and Florida's offensive line struggling in recent weeks. But the Gators still have plenty of talent, especially on the offensive side, and The Swamp is one of the toughest environments in college football. That's a tough position for a reeling team to be placed in. The game will be close into the second half but the Gators figure to pull away and hand Oklahoma its second consecutive defeat. Final: Florida 24, Oklahoma 14 Brady Trantham A new offensive coordinator doesn'tchange the fact that John Mateer is still QB1 at OU. Mateer gives Oklahoma their best shot in any game, but in 20 games as the Sooner signal caller, it is apparent that he simply isn't very good. A coaching change can, in theory, help him in spots, but if OU needs their QB to make a play in a tight game, chances are he will make that play - just for the other team. Florida sticks to the run and gets Oklahoma on a few explosives and rides it to an easy win. picks.headline: Sooners Wire Staff Predictions for Oklahoma vs. Florida
picks.blurb: Sooners Wire Staff Predictions for Oklahoma vs. Florida - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL news, live updates Misiorowski, Schlittler win Cy Youngs NFL midseason awards Rex Ryan arrested Skubal suitors emerge Sooners Wire Staff Predictions for Oklahoma vs. Florida Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Oklahoma Sooners are heading down to Gainesville, Fla., for the first time ever to take on the Florida Gators . The Sooners need to win two of their final four to earn bowl eligibility . With a new voice leading the offense, the Sooners are hoping for a turnaround to end the 2026 season. Jason Witten takes over an offense that has underachieved this season, given the number of returning starters along the offensive line and the weapons at returning quarterback John Mateer. How much better can Oklahoma be in a week is the question on everyone's minds. It's unlikely the Sooners will suddenly erupt on offense, but if they find more consistency, they'll have a chance to finish the season on a high note. So how will the Sooners perform in "The Swamp?" Our staff here at Sooners Wire picked this week's showdown between the Sooners and the Gators. Too Many Questions Oklahoma tight ends coach Jason Witten, left, talks with coach Brent Venables during a Sooners football spring practice in Norman, Okla., Thursday, April 9, 2026. There are just too many moving parts for Oklahoma to reliably believe the Sooners could win a road game in the swamp. The Sooners have made a change at offensive coordinator and the availability of a bunch of notable players on both sides of the ball are still in question. There's also the question of how Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer will play without Ben Arbuckle on the sideline for the first time in years. Even though Florida has a few issues to worry about as well, they're certainly not as dire as Oklahoma's at the moment. Florida 21, Oklahoma 10 James D. Jackson, Contributor Improved Sooners Touchdowns? Touchdowns. Oklahoma made a huge move this week by letting go of Ben Arbuckle and having Jason Witten call plays. Witten called plays as a high school head coach and had a ton of success doing it. I think the offense will play with a fire we haven't seen this year, and the defense will return to its dominant ways. Because of that, I've got OU winning and the offense scoring three touchdowns. OU 27, Florida 17 Oklahoma 27, Florida 17 Jaron Spor, Contributor Defense gives Oklahoma a chance Sep 4, 2026; Norman, Oklahoma, USA; UTEP Miners quarterback EJ Colson Jr. (1) throws as Oklahoma Sooners defensive lineman David Stone (0) chases during the game at Gaylord Family-Oklahoma Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Last week's disaster set in motion a sequence of events that should end with Brent Venables' team having a new offensive coaching staff, a new starting QB, and new faces up and down the offensive depth chart. For now, though, the only change is the absence of OC Ben Arbuckle, so all of Oklahoma's other offensive problems remain. Expect OU's defense to bounce back against Florida, but expect the offense to continue faltering for the remainder of this season. Florida 16, Oklahoma 7 Aaron Gelvin, Contributor Promising, but Sooners struggle Oct 31, 2026; Norman, Oklahoma, USA; Oklahoma Sooners quarterback John Mateer (10) throws during the first quarter against the South Carolina Gamecocks at Gaylord Family-Oklahoma Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images As much as I'd like to believe that things are going to magically turn around, it's hard to create that expectation. Jason Witten may be the answer to what ails John Mateer and the Oklahoma Sooners offense. However, until we see it, there's no telling what you'll get from Witten's crew. Expect the defense to bounce back and play well against Jaden Baugh and the Gators' rushing attack, but with injury concerns in the secondary, the Sooners may have a hard time slowing down Tramell Jones. Florida is a one-touchdown favorite on its home field to start the week and if the team plays the way it did against the likes of Ole Miss and Texas, this should be a sure win. Defensive end Kam Franklin and safety Sharif Denson are questionable on the initial report, released at 7:10 p.m. CT on Wednesday. Safety MJ Preston is doubtful.
